Consider this unsynchronized function, called concurrently by threads A and B against the SAME dictionary, initially stock["n"] = 6. Each thread calls reserve(stock, 4). Treat each labeled operation as atomic; the scheduler can switch only between the labels. Each thread has its own local current.

def reserve(stock, quantity):
    current = stock["n"]          # read
    if current < quantity:        # check
        return False
    stock["n"] = current-quantity # write; then return True

Give ONE valid six-event interleaving in which BOTH calls return True, even though only 6 units existed. An event is "A.read", "A.check", "A.write", or the equivalent for B. Include all six once, respecting each thread's read/check/write order. A thread whose check fails cannot write. Report the resulting shared final_stock, successful_reservations, and oversell_amount = max(0, total approved quantity - initial stock).
Choose safe_fix from exactly: "lock-write-only" (lock just the assignment); "whole-function-lock" (one shared lock covers read, check and write); "thread-local-lock" (each call makes its own lock); "retry-return-false" (perform the same write but return False). Choose the fix that prevents this accounting race without falsely denying successful reservations.
Finally, with that correct shared-lock behavior and a fresh stock of 6, run quantities [2,5,1] sequentially in that order, returning each boolean result and the final stock.
Return JSON only, with exactly this shape: {"interleaving":[six event strings],"final_stock":integer,"successful_reservations":integer,"oversell_amount":integer,"safe_fix":"one choice","atomic_sequential":{"results":[three booleans],"final_stock":integer}}.

Choose and schedule jobs to MAXIMIZE their total value, subject to all constraints. There is one CPU and one GPU, each able to run at most one job at a time. Jobs are non-preemptive and use only their named resource. Every start time is a nonnegative integer. Every chosen job must finish by time 6. A job may start exactly when a prerequisite finishes. All prerequisites of a chosen job must also be chosen and completed first. Jobs A and B are mandatory and must both start at time 0; all other jobs are optional. Every job can run at most once. Unscheduled jobs earn no value. There is no secondary makespan objective.
Jobs (id, resource, duration, value, prerequisites):
A, CPU, 2, 0, none
B, GPU, 1, 0, none
C, CPU, 2, 7, A
D, GPU, 2, 8, A,B
E, CPU, 1, 5, B
F, GPU, 2, 9, C
G, CPU, 2, 10, D
H, GPU, 1, 6, E
I, CPU, 1, 4, H
J, GPU, 1, 12, I
K, CPU, 1, 6, D
L, GPU, 1, 5, C
Return only a JSON object with exactly these keys: {"schedule":[{"job":"ID","start":integer},...],"total_value":integer,"makespan":integer}. Include every chosen job once, including A and B. total_value is the sum of chosen job values, and makespan is the latest finish time. Any globally optimal feasible schedule is accepted.
